newsitem.title: UK: IBCA affirms J Sainsbury ratings.
newsitem.headline: IBCA affirms J Sainsbury ratings.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Friday it had affirmed J Sainsbury Plc's AA minus long-term and A1 plus short-term ratings.

"J Sainsbury (JS) has today issued a trading statement for the 16 weeks to January 11, 1997 which warns of a further fall in pre-tax profits (PBT) in the financial year ending 1997," IBCA said in a statement.

IBCA said PBT, which fell by 12 percent to 712 million stg in the financial year ending 1996 was expected to fall by about a further 10 percent in the financial year to 1997 to between 640 million stg to 650 million stg.
"JS will also make a futher 50 million stg provision for the ongoing integration of the Texas DIY business acquired from Ladbroke during the financial year to 1996," IBCA said.

It said although the core UK food retailing business, Sainsbury Supermarkets, had seen a return to positive volume growth of 7.0 percent (up 4.0 percent on a like-for-like basis), this has not come without a fall in gross margins.

"The cost of the introduction for the Extra Reward Points scheme and improving product availability and customer service, all aimed at boosting sales performance in the face of a strong challenge from rival UK supermarket groups has resulted in the fall in profits," the rating agency said.

"The cost of regaining market share lost to its major rivals has clearly been higher than JS had previously anticipated. The UK food retail market will continue to be highly competitive and a further slip in gross margins cannot be ruled out," IBCA said.
IBCA downgraded the long term rating for JS from AA to AA- (AA minus) at the end of November 1996 as a reflection of the increased competitive pressure exerted upon JS.
"No further rating action is to be taken as a result of today's trading statement but the ongoing performance of all the leading UK food retailers will continue to be closely monitored," IBCA said.
